corruption.title: Corruption
corruption.dek: Three plain questions about public power and private benefit, each answered by its own deep dive.
intro: Corruption, as these pages use the word, means public power used for private or personal benefit. That is a definition, not a verdict. Each dive below takes one question, lays out the record in order, sets the explanations against the documents, and keeps its opinion in a labeled take.
A policy you disagree with is not corruption. Neither is a building you dislike. The question in each case is who benefits, who pays, and whether the rules meant to keep those apart were followed.

questions.q: Is he profiting from the office?
questions.text: Money reaching the president and his family while he holds office: crypto ventures, stock trades, foreign deals and spending at his own properties.
Companies with business before the government paying for the president's own projects, and what they have received from the government since.
Taxpayer money spent to put the president's face and message in front of the public.
